claims.text: This trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation under POL-RD-01. The trace runs 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km — an excess of 5.98 km, which is 24.92% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern the threshold test, so the trip record's rounded 30.0 km convenience copy may not be cited for it.

The deviation is established but it is NOT material, so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is engaged on this trip: 5.98 km is below both material gates, 50% of optimal and 8.0 km absolute. The rider asks for no finding from either party's profile; POL-GEN-01 confines profiles to credibility weighting, and the rider's case rests on this trip's own trace and fare.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. The trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00111, and the pickup timestamp is consistent between the trip record (started 07:47:40) and the trace's first fix (07:47:40). The trace is unimpaired: 229 fixes, 10 s sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so no POL-RD-07(a) to (c) condition is engaged, and every artifact in the bundle carries weight_multiplier 1.0 so no POL-GEN-02 disclosure arises. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause; a bare assertion that traffic was bad discharges nothing.

On the booked optimal route the platform's own rate card produces SGD 31.00: base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 24.0 km (18.00) + 0.28 x 30.0 min (8.40) + the 0.80 platform fee, at the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown and nowhere else. The rider was charged SGD 37.74, SGD 6.74 above that figure — corroborating the rider's own account that this trip is never more than about $32 — and the POL-RD-02 refund measured against the booked optimal is SGD 6.74, rounded up to SGD 6.75.

The driver's explanation is an external traffic cause, so under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The rider accepts that EV-ADVIS-00111-01 is on file, complete and at full weight, so the comparison can be run; the driver's uncorroborated assertion in the counterparty_statement adds nothing to it, and the only question for the judge is whether the advisory satisfies each limb of POL-RD-03.

POL-RD-03 limb (c) — that the actual route left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it after — is not carried by any computed fact in this bundle. The only derived field that touches it is the advisory-area test, which measures whether the trace enters the advisory's own area, and the record itself says that test 'decides nothing by itself' because the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record. The exit and rejoin appear only in an assessor's narrative note, so the exoneration should not be treated as automatic.

The rider does not dispute the cap arithmetic: under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(5.98 km measured, 1.30 x (29.2 km shortest lawful alternative - 24.0 km booked optimal) + 1.0 km tolerance = 7.76 km). If the exoneration is made out in full, the whole excess is inside that cap, the closure-adjusted optimal becomes 29.98 km, and the fare breakdown's own closure computation gives a recomputed fare of SGD 37.585 against the SGD 37.74 charged — a residual of SGD 0.155, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis in POL-RD-02, which would move no money. The rider's contest is the limb (c) point above, not this arithmetic.

No part of the excess is attributable to a rider instruction. The chat log contains the driver's own announcement of his routing decision; the rider's single reply — 'as long as i reach by 8.30' — names no place and no road and carries a null waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04's instruction test and its 200 m corroboration test cannot be satisfied and nothing in the chat transfers the detour to the rider.

claims.text: The optimal route for this trip runs down the PIE: the routing engine's own note on the trip record says the optimal is 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound', and the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes exactly that corridor — 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit', all lanes, between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit. The advisory therefore names a road and expressway segment that the optimal route traverses, and the derived advisory test records intersects_route true and the trace entering the advisory area with 12 fixes inside it. POL-RD-03(a) is satisfied.

The advisory's validity window is 07:10 to 09:30 on 2026-08-03, and the GPS trace runs from first fix 07:47:40 to last fix 08:25:40 — the trace's whole span sits inside the closure window, with an overlap of 41.5 minutes and the advisory's own note confirming overlaps_trip_window true. The trace would have reached the affected PIE segment mid-trip, well within POL-RD-03(b)'s 15-minute buffer at each end.

The route the vehicle actually drove leaves the optimal corridor before the closed segment and rejoins it after: the driver came off at Bukit Panjang ahead of the Clementi Rd closure and rejoined on the AYE, which is the signed diversion the advisory itself records ('Diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd'). The trace's measured length, 29.98 km, tracks the advisory's own shortest lawful alternative of 29.2 km rather than any unrelated detour. POL-RD-03(c) is satisfied on the record; the contemporaneous counterparty statement puts the same route on file.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the entire deviation. The justified excess is the lesser of the measured excess (5.98 km on the trace) and 1.30 x (shortest lawful alternative 29.2 km - booked optimal 24.0 km) + 1.00 km of tolerance = 7.76 km. 5.98 is the lesser, so the closure-adjusted optimal is 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km against a measured 29.98 km. Nothing remains beyond the cap to refund.

Run the POL-RD-02 arithmetic against that closure-adjusted optimal and the residual is de minimis. The closure-adjusted duration is the booked 30.0 minutes scaled by 29.98/24.0 = 37.5 minutes, giving a recomputed fare of (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) + 0.80 = 37.585. Charged total is 37.74, so the residual refund is 0.155 — below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor, which the fare artifact's own closure block records as below_de_minimis true, payable 0.00. On this branch the outcome is NO_ACTION.

The driver announced the closure in the in-app chat at 07:54:20 — 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — before completing the diversion, and the rider read it at 07:54:48 and replied at 07:54:55, 'as long as i reach by 8.30', without objecting. That contemporaneous exchange corroborates the external-cause account and undercuts the claim text's assertion that there was no closure to be seen; the rider was told of it in real time and raised no objection.

The rider carries the initial burden and has shown an excess above the POL-RD-01 threshold — 5.98 km and 24.9% over a 24.0 km optimal, on a trace that is unimpaired. But the burden then shifts to the driver on an exculpatory clause, and the driver discharges it by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause: traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 and POL-RD-03. That is precisely what POL-RD-08 requires; the rider's bare assertion of an unexplained detour is not an answer to a cited advisory.

The trace that carries this finding is fully intact: 229 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds across the whole disputed segment. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) therefore do not fire, the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, and no independent corroboration is needed — the route finding rests on clean telemetry, with the advisory as an independent corroborating record in any event.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to uplift the remedy. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 588 completed trips in the same window, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test — a count of 3 or more, or a ratio of 0.05 or more — is met. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral follows. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is a different field and, under POL-GEN-01, cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure this test names.

This is a metered trip: fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote route does not apply and the dispute is governed by POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route. That computation, set out above, produces a residual below the de-minimis floor, and the fare lines themselves reconcile to the cent with tolls_erp at 0.00 and no ERP gantry on either route at this hour, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to add.

One point the record does not support on the driver's side, stated plainly: the billed distance of 30.0 km is not less than the trace's 29.98 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION arises under POL-RD-04. The driver's recovery on this trip is the fare as charged, which the closure exoneration leaves standing.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties:

A deviation did occur on this trip, and the rider is right about that much. The GPS trace for TRP-00111 (EV-GPS-00111) runs 29.98 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 24.0 km (EV-TRIP-00111) — an excess of 5.98 km, 24.9% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) are passed. The trace is unimpaired — 229 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps — so it governs the threshold test under POL-RD-01 and not the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record.

That deviation is nonetheless exonerated, on the driver's side, by a genuine road closure under POL-RD-03, and all three limbs are met:
(a) LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00111-01 closes the 'Pan Island Expressway (PIE) towards Tuas, after Clementi Rd exit', all lanes between Clementi Rd and Jalan Anak Bukit — a segment the booked optimal route uses, since the routing note reads 'BKE southbound then PIE westbound'.
(b) The advisory ran 07:10 to 09:30 on 3 August 2026; the trace runs 07:47:40 to 08:25:40, wholly inside that window, overlapping by 41.5 minutes.
(c) The driver left the optimal corridor before the closed segment and rejoined after it. The chat log EV-CHAT-00111 records his message at 07:54:20 — 'boss PIE towards tuas closed, lorry fire. i come off at bukit panjang ok' — the trace enters the advisory area (12 fixes inside it), and the distance driven, 29.98 km, matches the advisory's shortest lawful alternative of 29.2 km rather than an unexplained detour. The rider's point that limb (c) rests on no single derived field is noted, but the unimpaired trace is itself the carrier, and the advisory's own record of the signed diversion via Upper Bukit Timah Rd matches what was driven.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the whole deviation. Justified excess = min(5.98 km measured, 1.30 x (29.2 - 24.0) + 1.0 tolerance = 7.76 km) = 5.98 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is therefore 24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km with a duration of 30.0 x (29.98/24.0) = 37.5 minutes. Running POL-RD-02 against that adjusted route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 37.585 against the SGD 37.74 actually charged, a residual of SGD 0.155. That is below the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor in POL-RD-02, so no refund issues. This answers the rider's figure of SGD 6.75: once POL-RD-03 excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 must be computed against the closure-adjusted optimal, not the booked one, and on that route nothing refundable remains.

The remaining claims do not change the outcome. No part of the excess is a rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 — the rider's reply 'as long as i reach by 8.30' names no place or road and carries no waypoint — and there is no unbilled-distance shortfall (billed 30.0 km against a 29.98 km trace), so no driver compensation arises. There is no repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 588 completed trips, so POL-RD-06 neither uplifts the remedy nor generates a conduct referral, and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used. The fare is metered (fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not apply. There are no ERP lines, no gantries and no surcharges, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct.

No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: the trip identifiers match across the three instruments, the timestamps agree, the trace is not impaired, the advisory is on file at full weight, and the refund is nil. The monetary effect is nil and so sits below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold. The claim is not supported, the present state stands, and no money moves. Either party may still ask for a human review under POL-GEN-04.
